candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Determine a common denominator and rewrite fraction parts as equivalent fractions before subtraction when the denominators differ.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S01, B.S01, and C.S01 all describe the same prerequisite operation of creating like denominators through equivalent-fraction conversion before subtraction.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Rewrite a whole number or a mixed number with an improper fractional part into a subtraction-ready form without changing its value.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S02 and C.S02 each combine two normalization cases: rewriting a whole number as a whole plus 0 over a denominator, and converting a mixed number with an improper fractional part to standard mixed form. B splits this same broader concept into B.S02 (improper mixed-number normalization) and B.S03 (rewrite whole as mixed), so both map here as a one-to-many alignment.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Subtract fractions with a common denominator and/or subtract the whole and fractional parts of mixed numbers once the forms are aligned.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: All three experts describe the core subtraction step performed after denominator matching or other preparatory rewriting is complete.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Regroup one whole as a fraction with the current denominator and adjust the whole part to complete subtraction when the fractional part would otherwise be negative.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S04, B.S05, and C.S04 all refer to the same regrouping/borrowing operation used in mixed-number or whole-minus-fraction subtraction.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Reduce a fractional result to lowest terms or simplify a zero-valued fraction or zero-fraction expression to an integer or whole-number result.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: These three skills all cover post-subtraction simplification, including fraction reduction and simplifying zero-fraction outcomes.

candidate_skills.canonical_definition: Combine the computed whole part and fractional part into the final mixed number, fraction, or integer answer.
candidate_skills.alignment_notes: A.S06 and B.S07 both isolate the final recombination/answer-formatting step after subtraction. C has no separate skill for this; its codebook appears to absorb final presentation into other steps rather than treating it as a distinct concept.

alignment_summary: The three codebooks align strongly on five core concepts: finding common denominators, normalization before subtraction, subtracting aligned parts, borrowing/regrouping, and simplifying results. The main structural difference is that Expert B splits normalization into two narrower skills, while Experts A and C combine them into one broader normalization concept. Experts A and B also separately identify final recombination into answer form, whereas Expert C does not treat that as a standalone skill. Every skill_id from all three experts has been mapped exactly once.
